study type: Cross-sectional study nested in a cohort
exposure: need for intensive care unit admission
cohort: The study included 509 mother-child dyads where mothers were adolescents (13-19 years) and their children were assessed for malocclusion between 24 and 36 months of age.
finding: Children with no need for intensive care unit admission and those breastfed for 24 months or longer had a lower risk of malocclusion, whereas children with an Apgar score less than 7, and those who had used or were still using a pacifier, had a higher risk of malocclusion.
cross-section timing: When children were 24 to 36 months of age
